deck.topic: What actually surprises Texas transplants (SA, Austin, DFW)
deck.hook: The heat is not what breaks transplants here.

points.title: It Is The Drive
body: This is the part that actually breaks people. Ten miles in Texas is not ten miles anywhere else.
Buyers tour a house at noon on a Sunday and never see the same road at seven on a Tuesday.
points.loop: The map hides two more things.

points.title: Toll Roads Are Daily
body: Your phone will route you the fast way. In Austin and DFW especially, the fast way is often paid.
It is a small charge twice a day, five days a week, forever.
points.loop: Something else splits the same street.

points.title: School Lines Cut Houses
body: District boundaries were drawn decades ago and nobody redraws them to make sense.
Two houses across the road from each other can feed into completely different schools.
points.loop: Then January brings its own envelope.

points.title: No Income Tax, But
body: The money comes back through property tax, and the rate depends on your county, your city, and your school district.
Notices land in spring. The real bill lands at the end of the year.
points.loop: Year two is where it stings.

points.title: Hail, Not Heat
body: Heat is boring. You run the AC and move on with your life.
It is hail and the winter freeze that hit insurance premiums, and the age of the roof decides how bad.
points.loop: One choice makes all of this easier.

points.title: Choose By Saturday
body: San Antonio, Austin and DFW are three different lives, not three versions of the same one.
Most people compare listings first and lifestyle second. That is backwards.
points.loop: Most people pick this the wrong way round.

linkedinCaption:
Most out of state buyers I work with arrive with a spreadsheet of listings and no sense of what daily life here actually costs them.

The surprises are rarely the house. It is the drive at seven on a Tuesday versus noon on a Sunday. It is toll roads becoming a fixed part of the commute. It is school boundaries that split neighbors across the road. It is property tax rates that shift by county, city and district. It is hail and freeze driving insurance, not heat.

San Antonio, Austin and DFW are three different lives. Compare the Saturday first, then the listings.

For those of you advising relocating clients, what do you find they underestimate most?
